data.narrative:
Tempo is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Nima Rahmatian, Kelvin Randhir, Joerg Petrasch, and Alessandro Bo. The target sector comprises nine identified peers across Climate & Energy, including both public (1 company: LNZA) and private (8 companies) entities. Notable private comparables include Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBolt Metals, and Electric Hydrogen. However, the narrow peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with similar valuation characteristics to support a robust peer-median approach.

Valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, the only applicable triangulation method given data constraints. Using total capital raised of $50M as a value proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression yields an implied valuation of $100M. This method treats the aggregate capital deployed as a baseline and reflects expected value creation between Series A and subsequent funding rounds.

The triangulated valuation range is $85M (low), $100M (median), and $115M (high). Key uncertainties stem from limited peer comparability; the absence of three or more direct same-stage or adjacent-stage peers prevents calibration against market multiples and relative metrics. A broader peer dataset at Series B or later stages, or more granular stage-specific comps, would strengthen conviction. The single-method foundation also limits cross-validation. Decision-makers should treat this range as preliminary and conditional on higher-fidelity peer data becoming available.
